section_summary: This section follows French bondholders’ efforts to secure sterling-equivalent payment on the City of Tokyo’s 1912 loan, from a 1931 French court ruling through a 1933 appeal and a 1939 settlement. It also includes a contemporary article on Haiti’s prewar loans, two handwritten notes, a search form, and a departmental file note.

subfiles.title: Paris despatch on the Tokyo loan ruling and gold-payment disputes
subfiles.from: Walter E. Edge, U.S. Embassy, Paris
subfiles.about: Reports a French high-court ruling on the Tokyo loan and discusses Haitian and French bond-payment disputes.
subfiles.summary: The despatch says Tokyo’s 1912 loan must be serviced in sterling or equivalent francs. It also forwards an article on Haitian gold-loan claims and notes France’s refusal to reconsider payments to British holders of French bonds.

subfiles.title: L’Information: City of Tokyo bonds and Court of Cassation rulings
subfiles.about: Prints the French Court of Cassation’s rulings on payment of the City of Tokyo’s 1912 loan.
subfiles.summary: The court treats the London, New York, and Paris tranches as one sterling-denominated loan and recognizes French holders’ right to equivalent payment. It does not establish a fixed gold value for the currencies.

subfiles.title: L’Information: Haitian loans
subfiles.about: Reviews Haiti’s finances and French creditors’ claims concerning prewar loans.
subfiles.summary: The article surveys Haiti’s debt, budgets, trade, and U.S. financial influence. It argues that holders of the 1910 gold loan have grounds to contest early repayment in depreciated paper francs.

subfiles.title: Paris despatch forwarding bondholders’ appeal
subfiles.from: Walter E. Edge, U.S. Embassy, Paris
subfiles.about: Forwards a French bondholders’ letter asking Tokyo to honor the court ruling.
subfiles.summary: Edge reports that bondholders seek prompt settlement and notes press speculation that Tokyo is negotiating a new 300-million-franc loan in Paris.

subfiles.title: L’Ami du Peuple: Appeal to the City of Tokyo
subfiles.about: Publishes a bondholders’ appeal for immediate payment at sterling parity.
subfiles.summary: Moizard’s January 27 letter urges Tokyo to accept the Court of Cassation ruling without further delay. The accompanying article discusses unpaid coupons and reports negotiations for a new Tokyo bond issue.

subfiles.title: Handwritten request concerning Osaka
subfiles.summary: A brief handwritten request for prompt information about Osaka.

subfiles.title: Economic Adviser handwritten note on Japan
subfiles.about: Discusses a departmental conclusion and planning concerning Japan.
subfiles.summary: The partly illegible note asks for a telephone update on the Department’s conclusion and mentions planning for Japan.

subfiles.title: Negative-report search form
subfiles.about: Lists record locations to check when reporting an unsuccessful file search.
subfiles.summary: Blank checklist for documenting searches of index cards, action papers, cartons, and file copies.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs note on Tokyo loan appeal
subfiles.about: Records the reported rejection of Tokyo’s appeal against sterling payment.
subfiles.summary: Notes the French ruling and possible further proceedings at The Hague.

subfiles.title: Paris despatch on the City of Tokyo loan appeal
subfiles.from: Walter E. Edge, U.S. Embassy, Paris
subfiles.about: Reports that France’s Court of Cassation rejected Tokyo’s appeal from the Dijon ruling.
subfiles.summary: The Dijon judgment required sterling rather than franc payment. Edge says French procedures appear exhausted, though a case before The Hague Court has been suggested.

subfiles.title: Paris despatch on the 1939 Tokyo loan settlement
subfiles.from: Maynard B. Barnes, for the Ambassador, U.S. Embassy
subfiles.about: Reports published terms of the December 20, 1939 agreement with French holders of Tokyo’s 1912 loan.
subfiles.summary: From September 1, 1940, Tokyo is to pay specified bonds and coupons in French francs. Eligible holders also receive new 5% securities redeemable over twenty-five years.
